name: Pare Hayashi-Amankwah
role: Electronic and physical observation expert — surveillance specialist
location: Dockside — Lake Michigan waterfront, smuggler territory
description:
Pare Hayashi-Amankwah is stocky and solid, with hands that look like they were built for breaking things and a face that confirms it. At 45, her expression defaults to a careful neutrality that took years of practice to maintain. The chrome is visible — synthetic blood with oxygen-carrying nanites — doesn't tire, heals faster — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She used to be somebody else, in another city, with another name — that person is officially dead, and Pare Hayashi-Amankwah plans to keep it that way. She works as a surveillance specialist out of Dockside, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Pare Hayashi-Amankwah has survived long enough in the runner game to be either very good or very lucky, and she cultivates ambiguity on the topic.

core_fears: Betrayal by someone they trust — the only currency that matters
Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it
The quiet — silence means something is about to go very wrong
core_desires: To protect the people in their district who can't protect themselves
A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts
To build something that outlasts the next contract cycle
coping_mechanisms: Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure
Planning — responds to chaos by making detailed contingency plans for everything
Violence — hits something when they can't process emotions, preferably something that deserves it
blind_spots: Believes their trauma makes them special instead of recognizing it as damage to manage
Mistakes pattern recognition for wisdom — sees connections that aren't there
Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
psychology.secret: Pare Hayashi-Amankwah has been doubling fees to clients and pocketing the difference. The fixer who handles their contracts doesn't know. Yet.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Educated vocabulary wrapped in street delivery — the contrast is deliberate.
speech_patterns.cadence: Low and even — the vocal equivalent of still water.
verbal_tics: Uses technical jargon for everything, including emotions
Whispers when angry — the quieter the voice, the worse the situation
example_lines: "I've been watching you for three days. You should close your curtains."
"Information is the only commodity that appreciates with age."
"Everyone thinks they're careful. Nobody is careful enough."

story_hooks: A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Pare Hayashi-Amankwah's reputation — and a price for silence
A high-paying contract turns out to target someone Pare Hayashi-Amankwah owes a personal debt to
Pare Hayashi-Amankwah's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad
narrative_function: Pare Hayashi-Amankwah functions as a connector — her work puts her in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving her naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
augmentations: Synthetic blood with oxygen-carrying nanites — doesn't tire, heals faster. Geneware muscle density treatment — looks natural, hits like chrome
daily_life: Between contracts, maintains a cover identity — mundane work, mundane hours, mundane neighbors. The transition from civilian to runner and back requires a conscious effort that gets easier with practice and more disturbing with self-awareness.
affiliation: Independent — known in Old Harbor circles

weaknesses: poor impulse control in specific triggers
risk-averse to the point of missed opportunities
augmentation dependency — performance drops sharply if chrome malfunctions

decision_rules: Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Always has an exit route planned before agreeing to any meeting
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — read the situation, identify threats and advantages
2. Negotiate — try to find a solution that doesn't cost ammunition
3. Intimidate — make the cost of conflict clear
4. Precision violence — surgical, targeted, minimal collateral
5. Full engagement — overwhelming force, no half measures
6. Emergency protocol — abort mission, survival priority, deal with consequences later

interpersonal_modes.employers: Professional and transactional. The relationship is defined by the contract and nothing else.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Competitive but reliable. Will challenge decisions but never abandon the team.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Superficially friendly, internally cataloguing exits and weapons. The smile is real; the relaxation isn't.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Heightened awareness, sharper focus. Low stress is fuel.
stress_responses.medium: Withdrawal. Conversations become monosyllabic. Focus narrows to the immediate problem.
stress_responses.high: Controlled aggression. The training takes over. Emotions are packed into a box for later.
stress_responses.critical: Disassociation. The body operates on training while the mind retreats to somewhere safe. Comes back disoriented.

contradictions: Projects confidence but makes decisions from a foundation of fear they've never examined
Claims to live in the present but is haunted by specific moments from the past that dictate current behavior
habits: Carries a specific caliber round as a lucky charm — has never fired it
Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
Wears the same item of clothing for luck — a scarf, a glove, a specific pair of boots
Never drinks anything they didn't see poured or open themselves
breaking_points: Being publicly exposed — name, face, address, all of it blown
Watching someone they trained or mentored die on a job they recommended
